res: assay accepted: baseline median 3.45359, noise 5.9%. Wins must beat it by > 5.9%.

why:
I have a working BFS at 3.45 seconds, but a faster version would need to beat that by more than 5.9% to be worth the effort. I'm weighing whether numpy is available, and I'm also considering a bit-parallel BFS using Python big integers, since shifting and combining 1M-bit frontiers could be quick even at 1000x1000, though I'm not yet sure how the path length will affect it.

I'm wary of the bit-parallel idea here: a snake-like maze could need around 500k BFS levels, and each level touches a 125KB integer, so that would be far too slow. I'll drop that path and stick with the working 3.45-second BFS.
